clue.text: Vice seen in cold light

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a lamp is a source of light

explanation.surface: Some wickedness is exposed in the chilly glare of day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vice' reads as wickedness, but here it is the workshop tool that grips things.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a gripping tool, and a clamp is the same kind of holding device.

clue.text: Blair acted, in trouble, having graduated

indicators.note: something in trouble is in disarray, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tony Blair performed while in difficulties, after finishing his degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Graduated' suggests finishing university; here it means marked with a measuring scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A gauge marked off in degrees or units has been set to a scale, which is what graduated means.

clue.text: Sailors get two-thirds of 18 and find "zero", perhaps

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman, a crossword staple for sailor

indicators.note: two-thirds of a nine-letter word leaves six letters, so its first three are dropped

parts.note: the answer to 18 Across, a word meaning degenerate

explanation.surface: Seamen take most of another answer and discover nothingness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two-thirds of' keeps the last six of the nine letters of 18 Across. The definition is a word that can come before zero, as in the lowest possible temperature.
explanation.definitionFit: Absolute zero is the coldest possible temperature, so zero is an example of something so described.

clue.text: Looter's flipping cheek over beer

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word for cheek is read backwards

parts.note: lip is impudence, as in don't give me any lip
lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A thief has the infernal nerve to demand a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild curse; it reverses LIP to PIL. 'Over' places it above LAGER in this down answer. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plunders and steals goods in wartime or riots is a synonym for a looter.

clue.text: The winner is second

definitions.meaning: the person who comes first in a contest
to second a cause is to back or support it

explanation.surface: A paradox: the victor turns out to be runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like a placing behind the winner; it is the verb meaning to back or support.
explanation.definitionFit: A title-holder is the victor, and as a verb it means to support or speak up for a cause.

clue.text: Actors status is diminished

indicators.note: diminished means made smaller, so the word for status loses its last letter

parts.note: caste is social rank or class

explanation.surface: The performers find their standing reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: CASTE, social class, is shortened by its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The performers in a play or film are collectively known as its company or line-up.

clue.text: Wool that's almost worth putting back on

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: merit means worth or value

indicators.note: putting back means turning round, so the little word on is read backwards

explanation.surface: Some wool that is nearly worth wearing again.
explanation.walkthrough: MERIT loses its T to give MERI, then ON reversed gives NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Merino is a breed of sheep prized for its fine fleece, and the fibre takes its name.

clue.text: At home, male dog is protected from attack

indicators.note: protected means enclosed or shielded, so the male dog goes inside the word for at home

parts.note: in means at home
a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A male dog kept indoors is safe from assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is protected' means the male dog is shielded by the outer word. 'Attack' is a verb here, to challenge or assail.
explanation.definitionFit: To impugn is to challenge the truth or honesty of something, an attack in words.

clue.text: An element of energy put into French denial

indicators.note: put into means placed inside, so energy goes within the French word

parts.note: non is French for no
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Some power has been inserted into a Gallic refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: E goes inside NON.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a noble gas, number ten in the periodic table of chemical elements.

clue.text: Left first, not as dispirited

parts.note: 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I
less means not as much

explanation.surface: Someone who left before the rest, looking less than cheerful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First' is written 1ST; read the numeral 1 as the letter I to get IST.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without energy or enthusiasm, as a dispirited person is, is the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Quiet diplomacy admits single vessel

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: tact is skill in handling people delicately
I is the Roman numeral for one
an urn is a vase or container

explanation.surface: Discreet negotiation lets in just one ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a container. 'Admits' puts I inside TACT to give TACIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved person who says little is described this way, a synonym for uncommunicative.

clue.text: Tried to follow a source of trouble and gave evidence

indicators.note: to follow means to come after, so this word goes after the earlier pieces
the source of something is its beginning, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: tested means tried out

explanation.surface: Someone tried to trace the origin of a problem and testified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tried' suggests a court case, but it is just tested. A and the first letter of trouble come before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To attest is to bear witness or certify that something is true, as a witness does in court.

clue.text: Daring to accept city runs post!

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the city and runs go inside the word for daring

parts.note: bold means daring or brave
LA is Los Angeles
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a bold venture taking on a city in record time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To accept' puts the city and runs inside the word for daring, after its third letter. 'Post' is a noun, a short thick pillar, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A short stout pillar, as on a quayside or by a road, is this kind of post.

clue.text: Trap is set — sure doom for him!

definitions.text: Trap is set — sure doom for him!

indicators.note: to set something is to arrange it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trap is primed, and the creature it catches is done for.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a small rodent facing a set trap, while 'is set' rearranges SURE DOOM.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormouse is a small rodent, exactly the kind of creature for which a set trap spells the end.

clue.text: Resolve to go, using expenses

indicators.note: to resolve is to break into parts again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A determination to leave, spending money as you go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resolve' seems to mean decide; it signals that the letters of TO GO USING are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Money spent out of a budget is a synonym for costs or expenditure.

clue.text: Diverts team and follows

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
tracks means follows or trails

explanation.surface: A coach redirects the squad and shadows them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Follows' looks like a link; it gives TRACKS.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone away from their main purpose is to distract them, a synonym for diverts.

clue.text: Damned heliports made a mess of Canaan!

indicators.note: messing something up jumbles it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wretched helicopter pads have ruined the biblical land.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram uses all fifteen letters of DAMNED HELIPORTS.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Canaan is the country God pledged to Abraham's descendants.

clue.text: Daily construction at north Greenwich — the way one originally conceived

parts.note: the Millennium Dome is the large tented building on the Greenwich peninsula in London
ST is street, a way
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A newspaper describes a London building as its designer first imagined it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' seems an adjective or a newspaper; in Britain a daily is a cleaner who comes in by the day.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage a daily is a cleaning help, a household servant, which is a synonym for a domestic.

clue.text: Broadcasts on a high, coming down to earth here

indicators.note: on means placed on top of, so in this down answer the first word goes above the next

parts.note: airs means broadcasts, as a programme is aired
a trip is a drug-induced high

explanation.surface: Programmes about a drug experience, ending with a return to reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming down to earth' suggests sobering up after a high; here it is aircraft landing.
explanation.definitionFit: A strip of ground where light aircraft land and take off is a place for touching down.

clue.text: Degenerate pervert sidles out

indicators.note: to pervert is to twist or distort, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A deviant creeps furtively out of the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pervert' looks like a noun for the shady figure, but it is a verb telling you to twist SIDLES OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A person given over to vice is depraved or debauched, a synonym.

clue.text: Communicate non-verbally with a student — that's impressive

parts.note: to sign is to communicate with hand gestures
L is a learner driver, a student

explanation.surface: Using hand signs with a pupil is a remarkable feat.
explanation.walkthrough: L for learner comes from the L-plate on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal achievement is a striking or notable one, so the adjective means remarkable.

clue.text: Source of oxygen equipment at home

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
a rig is a set of equipment
in means at home

explanation.surface: The supply of oxygen apparatus is kept in the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source' looks like part of the surface; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The point where something begins or comes from is its beginning or root.

clue.text: One helps an actor with some furniture

definitions.meaning: a backstage assistant who helps performers into their costumes
a sideboard or kitchen cabinet with shelves

explanation.surface: A theatre helper comes with a piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a costume assistant in the theatre and a sideboard with shelves go by this name.

clue.text: Setter perhaps tried to change, and became worn out

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of the following word are rearranged

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler attempted a change and ended up exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' invites the puzzle compiler, but it is the gun dog. 'To change' rearranges TRIED into TIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exhausted, completely drained of energy, is the meaning of this phrase.

clue.text: One's beaten by daughter with spirit

parts.note: rum is a spirit, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone is defeated by their daughter who has plenty of fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spirit' suggests courage, but it is the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument is struck with sticks, so it is a thing that gets beaten.

clue.text: Honey is expensive

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment, like darling

explanation.surface: The sweet stuff costs a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an affectionate address like sweetheart and a description of something costly.

clue.text: Mysterious drunkard found in east Morecambe

indicators.note: found in means placed inside, so the drunkard sits within the other pieces

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, of the double act Morecambe and Wise
a sot is a habitual drinker

explanation.surface: A boozer is discovered on the eastern side of a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire seaside resort, but it is the comedian Eric Morecambe. 'Found in' puts the drunkard between east and the comedian's first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood only by a select few is obscure or arcane, a synonym.

clue.text: To shirk is a bit abnormal in Germany

indicators.note: a bit means a portion, so the answer is a run of letters inside these words

explanation.surface: Avoiding work is seen as rather unusual by the Germans.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across abnorMAL IN GERmany.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretending to be ill so as to avoid work is a specific way of dodging duty.

clue.text: Manages to instil energy into the police

indicators.note: into means placed inside, so energy goes within the word for police

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in putting fresh vigour into the force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Into' puts the energy symbol inside the word for police, just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal successfully with a difficulty, a synonym for get by.
